title: Combustion Analysis Flow Chart
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AP Chemistry
description: Interactive Mermaid flowchart of the combustion analysis procedure. Students step through ten boxes, from weighing the sample to the empirical formula, while a side panel works each calculation for the selected lab data and checks the result against a molar mass.

learningObjectives: Construct the step-by-step procedure for a combustion analysis problem
Evaluate whether a calculated empirical formula is consistent with a given molar mass
standards: AP Chemistry CED Unit 1: Atomic Structure and Properties (moles, molar mass, elemental composition of pure substances)

controls.label: Sample
controls.description: Chooses one of three sets of combustion data

controls.label: Previous
controls.description: Moves back one step in the flowchart

controls.label: Next
controls.description: Moves forward one step and reveals its calculation

assumptions: The compound contains only C, H, and O
Combustion is complete, so all C becomes CO2 and all H becomes H2O
Each value is rounded to four significant figures before the next step

keyQuestions: Why is the mass of oxygen found by subtraction?
Why does each mole of water account for two moles of hydrogen atoms?
What do you do when a mole ratio is not close to a whole number?
commonMisconceptions: Using 1.008 g instead of 2.016 g of hydrogen per mole of water
Trying to find oxygen from the oxygen in the carbon dioxide and water
Rounding a ratio such as 1.33 to 1 instead of multiplying all ratios by 3
assessmentOpportunities: Have students work Sample C on paper and use the MicroSim only to check the final formulas
